sections.heading: Paths in the moduli space of marked IHS manifolds
Moduli spaces of modular vector bundles

body.text:
## Introduction

Moduli spaces of sheaves on $K3$ surfaces are one of the richest sources
of examples of irreducible holomorphic symplectic (IHS, for short)
manifolds, and the aim of this paper is to construct higher-dimensional
analogues of this phenomenon. Let $Y$ be a projective IHS manifold of
$K3^{[n]}$-type, and let $w\in \mathrm{NS}(Y)$ be a primitive class.
Under explicit numerical assumptions on $w$, we construct modular vector
bundles on $Y$ whose first Chern class is a prescribed multiple of $w$,
and whose rank and discriminant are fixed by the construction. Then, for
a suitable polarisation $H$, we prove that these sheaves are
slope-stable and correspond to a whole connected component $X$ of the
moduli space (see Theorem [1](#thm_main_intro){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm_main_intro"}). Each such component is again an IHS
manifold of $K3^{[n]}$-type. Moreover, the corresponding universal
family induces a derived equivalence between $X$ and $Y$ and a Hodge
isometry $H^2(X,\mathbb{Q})\xrightarrow{\sim} H^2(Y,\mathbb{Q})$.

The geometry of moduli spaces of vector bundles on smooth projective
varieties of dimension greater than two is largely inaccessible. In the
case of $K3$ surfaces, the foundational work of Mukai [@Mukai1] shows
that, provided that the Mukai vector $v$ is primitive and the
polarisation is $v$-generic, moduli spaces of Gieseker-semistable
sheaves are smooth and carry a holomorphic symplectic form. Many
subsequent attempts to obtain general results for higher-dimensional IHS
manifolds impose suitable topological conditions designed to mirror
different aspects of the theory on $K3$ surfaces.

Verbitsky [@verbitsky-hyperholomorphic-bundles] introduced the notion of
*projectively hyperholomorphic* vector bundles. Roughly speaking, these
objects are vector bundles whose projectivisation deforms along a
twistor line as a fibration in projective spaces. This property
automatically holds for simple vector bundles on $K3$ surfaces, by
classical deformation theory (see [@ogrady-moduli-sheaves-hk Corollary
2.1.5]), but becomes more restrictive on higher-dimensional IHS
manifolds. Verbitsky showed that it is satisfied by polystable vector
bundles $E$, such that the induced Hermite--Einstein connection on
$\mathcal{E}nd(E)$ is compatible with all the complex structures on the
fixed twistor line. A remarkable feature of moduli spaces of
projectively hyperholomorphic bundles is that, if they are smooth, they
carry a holomorphic symplectic form,
[@verbitsky-hyperholomorphic-bundles Section 9].

On the other hand, O'Grady [@OG22] introduced the class of torsion-free
modular sheaves. A torsion-free sheaf $F$ on a $2n$-dimensional IHS
manifold $Y$ is *modular* if there is a constant $d(F)\in \mathbb{Q}$
such that, for all $\alpha\in H^2(Y,\mathbb{C})$, it holds
$$\begin{equation*}
        \int_Y \Delta(F)\cdot\alpha^{2n-2}=
        d(F)(2n-3)!!q_Y(\alpha)^{n-1},
\end{equation*}$$ where $q_Y(-)$ is the Beauville--Bogomolov--Fujiki
form and the class
$$\Delta(F)=2\mathrm{rk}(F)c_2(F)-(\mathrm{rk}(F)-1)c_1(F)^2 \in H^4(Y,\mathbb{Q})$$
is the *discriminant* of $F$. As observed by O'Grady, if $\Delta(F)$ is
a multiple of $c_2(Y)$, then $F$ is modular. All the known examples of
projectively hyperholomorphic sheaves satisfy this property. Moreover,
modular sheaves carry a wall-and-chamber decomposition of the ample
cone, depending only on their Chern character, parallel to the $K3$
surfaces case (see [@OG22 Section 3]).

The theory of projectively hyperholomorphic and modular sheaves has led
to several spectacular applications. One of the first was Markman's
proof of the Shafarevich conjecture for IHS manifolds of $K3^{[n]}$-type
(see [@markman]). Subsequently, Markman's techniques were used to obtain
new bounds for the period--index conjecture in [@hotchkissetal], and to
prove a version of the $\mathrm{D}$-equivalence conjecture in
[@dequivconj]. Furthermore, in [@zhang] Zhang uses related techniques to
study equivalences of twisted derived categories of IHS varieties of
$K3^{[n]}$-type.

Recent literature in this area has developed along two main lines: the
existence of modular vector bundles (both rigid and non-rigid, see
[@OG22], [@markmanstable], [@Fat24], [@FO24], [@FT25]) on IHS manifolds
of a fixed deformation type, and the subsequent construction of IHS
manifolds as moduli spaces of such objects. Markman [@markmanstable]
exhibited the first examples of non-rigid modular vector bundles on the
Hilbert scheme of $n$ points on a K3 surface, induced by stable vector
bundles on the underlying surface (Construction
[13](#example1){reference-type="ref" reference="example1"}). On the
other hand, a first substantial contribution to the second mentioned
research line was provided by the work [@Bot24a; @Bot24b] of Bottini, in
which the OG10 IHS manifold is constructed as a moduli space of modular
vector bundles on the Fano variety of lines on a smooth cubic fourfold.
Furthermore, very recently, O'Grady [@OGrady2026; @OG26c] studied moduli
spaces of modular vector bundles on manifolds of $K3^{[2]}$-type and
constructed components which are IHS manifolds of
$K3^{[(a^2+1)]}$-deformation type, for any integer $a\geq 1$.

The present work contributes to the second research line, aiming to
construct IHS manifolds as moduli spaces of vector bundles on IHS
manifolds. Let $Y$ be a projective IHS manifold of $K3^{[n]}$-type and
$w\in \mathrm{NS}(Y)$ a primitive class. Let
$\ell(w)\in(\mathbb{Z}/\mathrm{div}(w)\mathbb{Z})^*/\{\pm1\}$ denote the
class of the integer $m$ appearing in the decomposition
$g(w)=v+m\delta_{S^{[n]}}$ after parallel transport
$g\colon H^2(Y,\mathbb{Z})\to H^2(S,\mathbb{Z})\oplus \mathbb{Z}\delta_{S^{[n]}}$
to a Hilbert scheme $S^{[n]}$; this is well-defined by
Definition [33](#def_invariant){reference-type="ref"
reference="def_invariant"}. Then our main Theorem reads as follows:

::: {#thm_main_intro .mainthm}
**Theorem 1** (Theorem [37](#thm_main){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm_main"}). *Let $n\geq 2$ be an integer, let $Y$ be a
projective IHS manifold of $K3^{[n]}$-type and let
$w \in \mathrm{NS}(Y)$ be a primitive class. If $\mathrm{div}(w)$ is
odd, consider a positive even integer $r$ such that:*

1.  *$\left[\frac{r}{2}\right]=\ell(w)\in (\mathbb{Z}/\mathrm{div}(w)\mathbb{Z})^*/\{\pm 1\}$;*

2.  *$\frac{w^2}{2r}+ \frac{r}{4}(n-1)$ is a positive integer;*

3.  *$\frac{w^2}{2r}+ \frac{r}{4}(n-1)$ is coprime with $r$.*

*If $\mathrm{div}(w)$ is even, consider a positive integer $r\geq 3$
such that:*

1.  *$[r]=\ell(w)\in (\mathbb{Z}/\mathrm{div}(w)\mathbb{Z})^*/\{\pm 1\}$;*

2.  *$\frac{w^2}{2r} + r(n-1)$ is a positive integer;*

3.  *$\frac{w^2}{2r}$ is coprime with $r$.*

*Then, there exists a polarisation $H$ on $Y$ and a connected component
$X$ of the moduli space $M_{Y,H}$ of Gieseker $H$-semistable sheaves on
$Y$, such that*

1.  *$X$ is an IHS manifold of $K3^{[n]}$-type.*

2.  *$X$ parametrises $H$-slope stable modular vector bundles $E$ on $Y$
    with the following invariants:*

    ::: minipage
    *$$\begin{equation*}
            c_1(E)= \bigg\{\begin{array}{ll}
               r^{n-1}n! w  & \textit{if }\mathrm{div}(w) \textit{ is odd} \\
               r^{n-1}n! \frac{w}{2}  & \textit{if }\mathrm{div}(w) \textit{ is even}
            \end{array}
    \end{equation*}$$*
    :::

    ::: minipage
    *$$\begin{align*}
           \mathrm{rk}(E)&= r^n n!\\
            \Delta(E) &= \frac{(r^n n!)^2}{12}c_2(Y).
    \end{align*}$$*
    :::

3.  *The Fourier-Mukai transform
    $$\Phi_\mathcal{E}\colon \mathrm{D}^b(X) \to \mathrm{D}^b(Y)$$ with
    kernel $\mathcal{E}$ is an equivalence, where $\mathcal{E}$ is a
    universal family on $X\times Y$.*
:::

### Idea of proof {#idea-of-proof .unnumbered}

We exhibit moduli spaces by constructing the corresponding universal
families. This is achieved by deforming a class of projectively
hyperholomorphic vector bundles $\mathcal{U}^{[n]}$ on products of
Hilbert schemes $M^{[n]}\times S^{[n]}$, where $M$ is a moduli space of
isotropic slope-stable vector bundles on a K3 surface $S$, and hence is
itself a K3 surface. We deform $\mathcal{U}^{[n]}$, as a projectively
hyperholomorphic bundle, along diagonal twistor lines in the moduli
space of marked pairs, as in [@markman]. Under suitable numerical
conditions, for $Y$ of $K3^{[n]}$-type, we find $X$ of $K3^{[n]}$-type
such that $X\times Y$ carries a projectively hyperholomorphic vector
bundle $\mathcal{E}$ . This step is achieved by combining
lattice-theoretic arguments with Markman's monodromy description for
manifolds of $K3^{[n]}$-type. The derived equivalence
$\mathrm{D}^b(X)\xrightarrow{\sim} \mathrm{D}^b(Y)$, as well as the
Hodge isometry $H^2(X,\mathbb{Q})\xrightarrow{\sim} H^2(Y,\mathbb{Q})$
(see Corollary [3](#maincor3){reference-type="ref"
reference="maincor3"}), are part of Markman's package [@markman].
Finally, exploiting the symmetries of the Hermite--Einstein connection
on $\mathcal{E}nd(\mathcal{E})$, we show that there exists a
polarisation such that $\mathcal{E}|_{\{x\}\times Y}$ is slope stable
for all $x\in X$. It follows that $X$ is isomorphic to a component of
the moduli space and $\mathcal{E}$ is a universal family.

### Corollaries and open questions {#corollaries-and-open-questions .unnumbered}

The derived equivalence stated in Theorem
[1](#thm_main_intro){reference-type="ref" reference="thm_main_intro"}
allows us to compare the Hodge structures of $Y$ and the moduli space
$X$ appearing in the statement of the main result, using results in
[@paolo_huy; @markman]. The outcome is summarised in the two Corollaries
below.

::: maincor
**Corollary 2** (Corollary [39](#cor_1){reference-type="ref"
reference="cor_1"}). *In the setup of Theorem
[1](#thm_main_intro){reference-type="ref" reference="thm_main_intro"},
the correspondence $$\begin{equation*}
        \tau_{\mathcal{E}}\colon H^{\ast}(X,\mathbb{Q})\to H^{\ast}(Y,\mathbb{Q}),
\end{equation*}$$ defined by the class
$\mathrm{ch}(\mathcal{E})\sqrt{\operatorname{td}_{X\times Y}}$, is an
isomorphism of level zero Hodge structures
([\[HSuntwisted\]](#HSuntwisted){reference-type="ref"
reference="HSuntwisted"}) and an isometry with respect to the Mukai
pairing.*
:::

::: {#maincor3 .maincor}
**Corollary 3** (Corollary [42](#cor_2){reference-type="ref"
reference="cor_2"}). *In the setup of Theorem
[1](#thm_main_intro){reference-type="ref" reference="thm_main_intro"},
there is a rational Hodge isometry $$\begin{equation*}
         \psi_{\mathcal{E}}\colon H^2(X,\mathbb{Q})\xrightarrow{\sim} H^2(Y,\mathbb{Q})
\end{equation*}$$ which is a nontrivial rational multiple of the
composition $$\begin{equation*}
        H^2(X,\mathbb{Q})\xrightarrow{\cup c_2(X)^{n-1}}H^{4n-2}(X,\mathbb{Q})\overset{\phi_{\mathcal{E}}}{\longrightarrow}H^2(Y,\mathbb{Q})
\end{equation*}$$ where $\phi_{\mathcal{E}}$ is the correspondence
induced by $\kappa(\mathcal{E})\sqrt{\operatorname{td}_{X\times Y}}$.*
:::

Finally, in Section [4](#sec_examples){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec_examples"} we provide applications of Theorem
[1](#thm_main_intro){reference-type="ref" reference="thm_main_intro"}.
We denote by ${}^{n}\mathcal{M}_{m}^{(\gamma)}$ the moduli space of
polarised IHS varieties $(Y,h)$ of $K3^{[n]}$-type such that
$\mathrm{div}(h)=\gamma\in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$ and $h^2=2m\geq 2$. If
$\gamma=1$ or $\gamma=2$ and $n+m\equiv 1\pmod{4}$, then
${}^{n}\mathcal{M}_{m}^{(\gamma)}$ is irreducible of dimension 20 and
quasi-projective.

::: {#cor_intro_mainthm_alldim .maincor}
**Corollary 4** (Corollaries [44](#cor_div1){reference-type="ref"
reference="cor_div1"}, [46](#cor_div2){reference-type="ref"
reference="cor_div2"}). *Let $(Y,w)\in {}^{n}\mathcal{M}_{m}^{(1)}$
(resp. $(Y,w)\in {}^{n}\mathcal{M}_{m}^{(2)}$) and
$r\in 2\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1},k\in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$ such that $(k,r)=1$
and $m=r(2k-r/2(n-1))\geq 1$ (resp. $r\in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 3}$ such that
$k:w^2/(2r)\in \mathbb{Z}$ and $(r,k)=1$). Then, there there is a
polarisation $H$ on $Y$ and a connected component $X$ of the moduli
space $M_{Y,H}$ of Gieseker $H$-semistable sheaves on $Y$, such that*

1.  *$(X,\psi_{\mathcal{E}}(w))\in {}^{n}\mathcal{M}_{m}^{(1)}$ (resp.
    $(X, \psi_{\mathcal{E}}(w))\in {}^{n}\mathcal{M}_{m}^{(2)}$) for
    generic $Y$;*

2.  *$X$ parametrises $\mu_H$-stable vector bundles with of rank
    $r^n n!$, first Chern class $r^{n-1}n!w$ (resp. $r^{n-1}n!w/2$) and
    discriminant $\frac{(r^n n!)^2}{12}c_2(Y)$;*

3.  *$X$ and $Y$ are derived equivalent.*
:::

In particular, we study some examples of locally complete families of
$K3^{[2]}$-type.

::: maincor
**Corollary 5** (Beauville--Donagi, Debarre--Voisin, Iliev--Ranestad,
see Corollary [47](#cor_BD_DV_IR){reference-type="ref"
reference="cor_BD_DV_IR"}). *Let $(Y,w)$ be a polarised IHS manifold of
$K3^{[2]}$-type such $\mathrm{div}(w)=2$ and one of the following
holds:*

- *$w^2=6$,*

- *$w^2=22$,*

- *$w^2=38$.*

*Then there is an ample divisor $H$ on $Y$ and a connected component $X$
of the moduli space of Gieseker $H$-semistable sheaves such that $X$ is
of $K3^{[2]}$-type, derived equivalent to $Y$ and parametrises $H$-slope
stable vector bundles $E$ with*

- *$rk(E)=18,\quad c_1(E)=3h \quad \Delta(E)=27c_2(Y)$ in case $(a)$,*

- *$rk(E)=2\cdot11^2,\quad c_1(E)=11h\quad \Delta(E)=\frac{11^4}{3}c_2(Y)$
  in case $(b)$,*

- *$rk(E)=2\cdot19^2,\quad c_1(E)=19h,\quad \Delta(E)=\frac{19^4}{3}c_2(Y)$
  in case $(c)$.*
:::

Analogous conclusions are drawn in
Corollary [45](#cor_EPWsextic){reference-type="ref"
reference="cor_EPWsextic"} for the case of the EPW sextic.

In Corollary [4](#cor_intro_mainthm_alldim){reference-type="ref"
reference="cor_intro_mainthm_alldim"} we observe that the Chern
characters of the of the vector bundles in the moduli space $X$ do not
depend on the choice of $(Y,w)\in {}^{n}\mathcal{M}_m^{(\gamma)}$, hence
it is natural to ask about properties of the construction in families.
Let us consider the quasi-projective coarse moduli space
${}^{n}\mathcal{M}_m^{(\gamma)}$ of polarised IHS manifolds $(Y,w)$ of
$K3^{[n]}$-type with $\gamma\in \{1,2\}$ and $n+m\equiv 1 \pmod{4}$ if
$\gamma=2$.

::: mainquest
**Question 1**. Does the correspondence $Y\mapsto X(Y)$ define a
birational automorphism between moduli spaces
$$\mu\colon {}^{n}\mathcal{M}_m^{(\gamma)} \dashrightarrow { {}^{n}\mathcal{M}_{m}^{(\gamma)}}\;?$$
:::

The answer to the question is affirmative in the case of the EPW sextics
(see Corollary [45](#cor_EPWsextic){reference-type="ref"
reference="cor_EPWsextic"}, [@OG15 Section 4.2] and
[@kapustka-kapustka-derived-equivalent-hk4 Proposition 5.2]).

It is natural to ask to what extent the arguments of this paper can be
generalized. Although we do not pursue this direction here, we expect
that the same techniques can also produce moduli spaces of twisted
vector bundles (see Remark [54](#twistedmoduli){reference-type="ref"
reference="twistedmoduli"}). In a different direction, one possible
strategy would be to start from a broader class of projectively
hyperholomorphic vector bundles, generalising
Construction [13](#example1){reference-type="ref" reference="example1"}.

Let $Y_0$ be an IHS manifold endowed with a Kähler class $\omega_{Y_0}$,
and let $M$ be a fine moduli space of $\omega_{Y_0}$-slope stable
projectively hyperholomorphic vector bundles on $Y_0$. Assume that $M$
is smooth. Then $M$ carries a natural holomorphic symplectic form (see
[@verbitsky-hyperholomorphic-bundles] and [@Bot24b Section 7]). Let
$\mathcal E$ be the universal family on $M\times Y_0$. Suppose that the
cohomological correspondence $\psi_{\mathcal{E}}$ is a Hodge isometry
such that $\omega_M:=\psi_{\mathcal{E}}^{-1}(\omega_{Y_0})$ is a Kähler
class on $M$. The Kähler classes $\omega_M$ and $\omega_{Y_0}$ then
determine a diagonal hyperkähler structure on $M\times Y_0$. This leads
to the following question.

::: {#quest2 .mainquest}
**Question 2**. Is the vector bundle $\mathcal E$ projectively
hyperholomorphic with respect to the split Kähler class
$\mathrm{pr}_M^*\psi_{\mathcal E}^{-1}(\omega_{Y_0})+\mathrm{pr}_{Y_0}^*\omega_{Y_0}$
on $M\times Y_0$?
:::

An affirmative answer would allow one to deform $\mathcal E$ as a
projectively hyperholomorphic bundle along the corresponding diagonal
twistor line, and would therefore produce moduli spaces of possibly
twisted vector bundles on deformations of $Y_0$. It would be very
interesting to understand if the answer to
Question [2](#quest2){reference-type="ref" reference="quest2"} is
positive for the examples studied in [@krug-reede-zhang].

### Structure of the paper {#structure-of-the-paper .unnumbered}

In Section [1](#secprojhyperholo){reference-type="ref"
reference="secprojhyperholo"} we review the theory of projectively
hyperholomorphic vector bundles and provide a criterion for the
Fourier--Mukai kernel of a twisted derived equivalence to be a twisted
universal family for a moduli space. In
Section [2](#sec_admissible){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec_admissible"} we take advantage of the explicit
description of monodromy operators for IHS manifolds of $K3^{[n]}$-type
and prove some lattice theoretical Lemmata. These will translate into
conditions on the $K3^{[n]}-$type IHS manifolds to which Markman's and
Verbitsky's results can be applied. In
Section [3](#sec_mainthm){reference-type="ref" reference="sec_mainthm"}
we state and prove Theorem [1](#thm_main_intro){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm_main_intro"}. We conclude with
Section [4](#sec_examples){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec_examples"}, where we present examples to which
Theorem [1](#thm_main_intro){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm_main_intro"} applies. In the appendices we collect some
auxiliary results on hyperholomorphic vector bundles and on the
variation of slope stability in the Kähler cone.

### Notation {#notation .unnumbered}

Let $X$ be a complex manifold, and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf on $X$
in the analytic topology. We denote by
$H^*_{\mathrm{an}}(X,\mathcal{F})$ the corresponding sheaf cohomology.
If $R$ is a ring, we denote by $H^*(X,R)$ the singular cohomology of $X$
with coefficients in $R$. If $X$ is Kähler, we denote by
$\mathcal{K}_X\subset H^{1,1}(X)\cap H^2(X,\mathbb{R})$ the Kähler cone.

## Projectively hyperholomorphic bundles

The proof of our main result is based on the work of Markman on
projectively hyperholomorphic bundles (see [@markman]). In this Section,
we recall the main features that we need in our arguments. For other
expositions and applications of this theory, we refer to
[@dequivconj; @ogrady-moduli-sheaves-hk; @kapustka-kapustka-derived-equivalent-hk4].

### Verbitsky's deformability results

Let $X$ be an IHS manifold and let $E$ be a holomorphic vector bundle on
$X$. To every Kähler class $\omega \in \mathcal{K}_X$, one can associate
the twistor family $\mathcal{X} \rightarrow \mathbb{P}^1_\omega$, a
smooth and proper morphism of complex manifolds whose fibers are the
complex manifolds obtained by rotating the complex structure of $X$
within the hyperkähler structure determined by $\omega$ (see
[@Huy-HK-basic Section 1.13]). In order for $E$ to deform as a
holomorphic vector bundle over the whole twistor family, its Chern
classes must remain of Hodge type for all complex structures
parametrised by $\mathbb{P}^1_\omega$. Verbitsky proved that, provided
that $E$ is $\omega$-slope stable, this is the only obstruction. More
precisely, using the notation above, he gives the following definition.

::: df
**Definition 1**. A holomorphic vector bundle $E$ on an IHS manifold
$(X,\omega)$ equipped with a Kähler class $\omega$ is called
*$\omega$-stable hyperholomorphic* if it is $\omega$-slope stable and
its Chern classes $c_1(E)$ and $c_2(E)$ remain of Hodge type for all
complex structures in the twistor line $\mathbb{P}^1_\omega$.
:::

The following Theorem of Verbitsky is a strong deformability result for
such bundles.

::: {#verb .thm}
**Theorem 2** ([@verbitsky-hyperholomorphic-sheaves Theorem 3.19]). *If
$E$ is $\omega$-stable hyperholomorphic, then there exists a holomorphic
vector bundle $\widetilde{E}$ on the twistor family
$\mathcal{X}\rightarrow\mathbb{P}^1_\omega$ such that
$\widetilde{E}|_{\mathcal{X}_0}\simeq E$, where $\mathcal{X}_0$ denotes
the fiber corresponding to the original complex structure on $X$.*
:::

In other words, the Hodge-theoretic condition on $c_1(E)$ and $c_2(E)$
guarantees that the Hermite--Einstein connection on $E$ is compatible
with all complex structures in the twistor line. This produces a
holomorphic vector bundle on the total space of the twistor family whose
restriction to the original fiber is the given bundle $E$.

Verbitsky's result was generalised to Azumaya algebras in
[@markman_bbf]. We now recall the definitions needed to state Markman's
generalization.

::: df
**Definition 3**. An *Azumaya algebra* $\mathcal{A}$ of rank $r^2$ over
a complex manifold $X$ is a locally free coherent
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module, with a global section $1_\mathcal{A}$ and an
$\mathcal{O}_X$-linear associative multiplication
$m \colon \mathcal{A}\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X} \mathcal{A}\longrightarrow \mathcal{A}$
with identity $1_\mathcal{A}$, such that there exists an open covering
$\{U_i\}$ of $X$ and a collection of isomorphisms
$\eta_i \colon \mathcal{A}|_{U_i} \longrightarrow \mathcal{E}nd(F_i)$ of
unital associative algebras for some locally free
$\mathcal{O}_{U_i}$-module $F_i$ of rank $r$ over each $U_i$.
:::

::: rmk
*Remark 4*. For other models of Azumaya algebras, we refer to
[@van-bree-gholampour-jiang-kool-pgl-sl Section 2]. In particular, when
$X$ is a smooth projective variety, they correspond to Severi--Brauer
varieties.
:::

Analogously to the case of vector bundles, one can define $\omega$-slope
stability for Azumaya algebras (see [@markman_bbf Definition 6.5]). The
generalisation of Verbitsky's result then reads as follows:

::: {#deformingazumaya .thm}
**Theorem 5** ([@markman_bbf Corollary 6.12]). *Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an
$\omega$-slope stable Azumaya algebra on an IHS manifold $X$. Assume
moreover that $c_2(\mathcal{A})$ remains of Hodge type $(2,2)$ along the
$\omega$-twistor line, and that the first Chern class of every direct
summand of $\mathcal{A}$ vanishes. Then there exists an Azumaya algebra
$\widetilde{\mathcal{A}}$ on the twistor family
$\mathcal{X} \rightarrow \mathbb{P}^1_\omega$ such that
$\widetilde{\mathcal{A}}|_{\mathcal{X}_0} \simeq \mathcal{A}$, where
$\mathcal{X}_0$ denotes the fiber corresponding to the original complex
structure on $X$.*
:::

::: rmk
*Remark 6*. For simplicity, we stated Verbitsky's results in the context
of irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifolds, although his arguments
only require a hyperkähler structure. For the more general setting, we
refer to Appendix [5](#app_hyperholo){reference-type="ref"
reference="app_hyperholo"}. It is crucial to use this more general
definition, as we will work with projectively hyperholomorphic bundles
on a product of IHS manifolds, which is not itself irreducible
holomorphic symplectic, but can be endowed with a diagonal hyperkähler
structure (see [@markman Section 5.3]).
:::

### Invariants of Azumaya algebras

An Azumaya algebra $\mathcal{A}$ of rank $r^2$ on a complex manifold $X$
can be regarded as a $\operatorname{PGL}_r$-torsor. Via the boundary map
$H^1_{\mathrm{an}}(X,\operatorname{PGL}_r)\rightarrow H^2_{\mathrm{an}}(X,\mathcal{O}^\times_X)$,
it defines an element
$\alpha\in H^2_{\mathrm{an}}(X,\mathcal{O}^\times_X)$, called *Brauer
class*. It is always torsion and it has order dividing $r$. The group
$\mathrm{Br}'(X):=H^2_{\mathrm{an}}(X,\mathcal{O}^\times_X)_\mathrm{tors}$
is called *cohomological Brauer group*.

::: rmk
*Remark 7*. The *Brauer group* $\mathrm{Br}(X)$ is the group of Brauer
equivalence classes of Azumaya algebras on $X$ (see
[@schroer-analytic-brauer]). The construction above induces a natural
group isomorphism $\mathrm{Br}(X)\longrightarrow \mathrm{Br}'(X)$. This
map is known to be an isomorphism in many cases; for instance, in the
algebraic setting, it is an isomorphism for smooth projective varieties
by Gabber's Theorem (see [@dejong-gabber]). In general, however, the
Brauer group and the cohomological Brauer group need not be
automatically isomorphic. This distinction will not play any role here,
since all twists considered below arise from Azumaya algebras, and
therefore lie in the image of the natural map
$\mathrm{Br}(X)\longrightarrow \mathrm{Br}'(X)$.
:::

Let
$\alpha\in\mathrm{Br}'(X)=H^2_{\mathrm{an}}(X,\mathcal{O}_X^\times)_{\mathrm{tors}}$
be represented by a Čech $2$-cocycle $\{\alpha_{ijk}\}$ with respect to
an open cover $\{U_i\}$ of $X$.

::: df
**Definition 8**. An *$\alpha$-twisted locally free sheaf* is given by a
collection of locally free sheaves $F_i$ on $U_i$ and isomorphisms
$\varphi_{ij}\colon F_j|_{U_{ij}}\longrightarrow F_i|_{U_{ij}}$ such
that, on triple overlaps $U_{ijk}$, we have
$\varphi_{ij}\circ\varphi_{jk}\circ\varphi_{ki}=\alpha_{ijk}\cdot\operatorname{id}_{F_i}$.
:::

There is a correspondence between Azumaya algebras and twisted locally
free sheaves (or equivalently $\operatorname{PGL}_r$-bundles) (see
[@huybrechts-schroeer-brauer]). Given an $\alpha$-twisted vector bundle
$E$, it is easy to see that $\mathcal{E}nd(E)$ is an Azumaya algebra
with Brauer class $\alpha$. Conversely, given an Azumaya algebra
$\mathcal{A}$, by definition there exists an open cover $\{U_i\}$ of $X$
such that $\mathcal{A}|_{U_i} \simeq \mathcal{E}nd(E_i)$ for some vector
bundles $E_i$ on $U_i$. There are isomorphisms of algebras
$\phi_{ij}:\mathcal{E}nd(E_i)\rightarrow\mathcal{E}nd(E_j)$ that - up to
refining the covering - can be assumed to be induced by isomorphisms
$\overline{\phi}_{ij}\colon E_i\rightarrow E_j$, by the Skolem--Noether
Theorem. The twisted sheaf associated to $\mathcal{A}$ is uniquely
determined up to tensoring with an untwisted holomorphic line bundle.

We are interested in the case where $X$ is a compact Kähler manifold
whose odd integral cohomology groups vanish (e.g. an IHS manifold of
$K3^{[n]}$-type or a product of IHS manifolds of $K3^{[n]}$-type). In
this case, via the exponential sequence, there is an identification
$$\mathrm{Br}'(X)\simeq (H^2(X,\mathbb{Z})/\mathrm{Pic}(X))\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}.$$
In other words, any Brauer class can be represented by a rational
cohomology class $B\in H^2(X,\mathbb{Q})$, which we call a *$B$-field*.

::: rmk
*Remark 9*. Our main construction consists in deforming Azumaya algebras
as in Theorem [5](#deformingazumaya){reference-type="ref"
reference="deformingazumaya"}. Let $X_1, X_2$ be two deformation
equivalent projective IHS manifolds, and suppose that
$E_1\in\mathrm{Coh}(X_1)$ is an untwisted locally free sheaf. Under
deformation of the associated Azumaya algebra $\mathcal{E}nd(E_1)$, the
Chern classes of $E_1$ need not be preserved: if
$E_2\in\mathrm{Coh}(X_2)$ is an untwisted locally free sheaf obtained by
deforming $\mathcal{E}nd(E_1)$ along a chain of twistor paths from $X_1$
to $X_2$, then the Chern classes of $E_2$ need not be obtained from
those of $E_1$ by parallel transport, even after tensoring by a line
bundle on $X_2$. A simple example is provided by a line bundle $L$ on an
IHS manifold $X_1$. Then $\mathcal{E}nd(L)\simeq \mathcal{O}_X$, which
deforms trivially along any twistor family. Along a twistor family, one
can reach a projective manifold $X_2$ such that $c_1(L)$ is not
algebraic. On the other hand, it holds
$\mathcal{O}_{X_2}=\mathcal{E}nd(T)$ for any line bundle
$T\in \mathrm{Pic}(X_2)$. Hence $T$ is a deformation of $L$ as
projectively hyperholomorphic sheaves, but $c_1(T)-c_1(L)$ is not
algebraic on $X_2$.
:::

Motivated by the previous remark, we recall invariants that are better
behaved. Let $E$ be a twisted vector bundle of rank $r$ on a complex
manifold $X$. Since $E^{\otimes r}\otimes \det(E)^{-1}$ is an untwisted
vector bundle, we can define the class $$\begin{equation}
\label{eq_def_kappa}
    \kappa(E):=\sqrt[r]{\mathrm{ch}(E^{\otimes r}\otimes \det(E)^{-1})}\in H^*(X,\mathbb{Q}),
\end{equation}$$ where the $r$-th root is chosen to have degree-zero
component equal to $r$. Note that the Azumaya algebra $\mathcal{E}nd(E)$
determines $E$ up to twist by a holomorphic line bundle $L$ and
$\kappa(E\otimes L)=\kappa(E)$. Consequently, the class $\kappa(E)$
depends only on the Azumaya algebra $\mathcal{E}nd(E)$, and can be
regarded as an invariant of $\mathcal{E}nd(E)$.

::: {#stiefel-whitney .rmk}
*Remark 10*. Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an Azumaya algebra of rank $r^2$ on a
complex manifold $X$. It determines a $\operatorname{PGL}_r$-torsor,
hence $\mathcal{A}$ defines an element of
$H_{\mathrm{an}}^1(X,\operatorname{PGL}_r)$. The central extension of
sheaves of groups, in the analytic topology,
$$1 \rightarrow \mu_r \rightarrow \mathrm{SL}_r \rightarrow \operatorname{PGL}_r \rightarrow 1,$$
induces the boundary map
$\delta\colon H_{\mathrm{an}}^1(X,\operatorname{PGL}_r)\rightarrow H_{\mathrm{an}}^2(X,\mu_r)$.
As a consequence, we can associate to $\mathcal{A}$, the so-called
*Stiefel--Whitney class* $w(\mathcal{A}):=\delta(\mathcal{A})$. Since
$X$ is locally contractible and paracompact, there is a natural
identification
$H_{\mathrm{an}}^2(X,\mu_r)\simeq H^2(X,\mathbb{Z}/r\mathbb{Z})$. We
point out that the Stiefel--Whitney class appears in the work of
Căldăraru under the name of *topological twisting class* (see
[@caldararu-nonfine-k3 Section 4]). We recall below some fundamental
properties of this class.

1.  If $\mathcal{A}$ is an Azumaya algebra on a product of complex
    manifolds $X\times Y$, then for all $x\in X$, it holds
    $w(\mathcal{A}|_{\{x\}\times Y})=i_x^{*}w(\mathcal{A})$, where
    $i_x\colon \{x\}\times Y=Y\hookrightarrow X\times Y$ is the
    inclusion and
    $i_x^*\colon H^2(X\times Y,\mathbb{Z}/r\mathbb{Z})\rightarrow H^2(Y,\mathbb{Z}/r\mathbb{Z})$
    denotes the pull-back.

2.  The Stiefel--Whitney class remains constant in a deformation family
    of Azumaya algebras. More precisely, if $\mathcal{X}\rightarrow B$
    is a smooth and proper morphism of complex manifolds, with $B$
    simply connected, and $\mathcal{A}$ is an Azumaya algebra of rank
    $r^2$ on $\mathcal{X}$, then for all $b,b'\in B$, we have
    $w(\mathcal{A}_b)=w(\mathcal{A}_{b'})$ under the natural
    identification
    $H^2(\mathcal{X}_b,\mathbb{Z}/r\mathbb{Z})\simeq H^2(\mathcal{X}_{b'},\mathbb{Z}/r\mathbb{Z})$
    induced by parallel transport.

3.  If $\mathcal{E}$ is an untwisted locally free sheaf such that
    $\mathcal{E}nd(\mathcal{E})=\mathcal{A}$, then
    $w(\mathcal{A})=-\pi(c_1(\mathcal{E}))$, where
    $\pi\colon H^2(X,\mathbb{Z})\rightarrow H^2(X,\mathbb{Z}/r\mathbb{Z})$.
:::

::: {#rmk_trasp_c1 .rmk}
*Remark 11*. Let $X_1,X_2$ be two deformation equivalent projective IHS
manifolds. Suppose that an untwisted locally free sheaf
$E_2\in\mathrm{Coh}(X_2)$ of rank $r$ is obtained from an untwisted
locally free sheaf $E_1\in\mathrm{Coh}(X_1)$ by deforming the
corresponding Azumaya algebras along a chain of twistor paths. By $(2)$
and $(3)$ of the previous remark, we have $\pi(c_1(E_2))=\pi(c_1(E_1))$
under the natural identification
$H^2(X_2,\mathbb{Z}/r\mathbb{Z})\simeq H^2(X_1,\mathbb{Z}/r\mathbb{Z})$.
If the parallel transport of $c_1(E_1)$ is algebraic on $X_2$, this is
equivalent to $c_1(E_2)-c_1(E_1)\in r \mathrm{Pic}(X_2)$. Thus, after
replacing $E_2$ by $E_2\otimes L$ for a suitable
$L\in\mathrm{Pic}(X_2)$, we may assume that $c_1(E_2)=c_1(E_1)$, where
$c_1(E_1)$ is viewed on $X_2$ via parallel transport.
:::

We are ready to give the following definition. Let $(X,\omega)$ be an
IHS manifold with a fixed Kähler class.

::: df
**Definition 12**. A $\omega$-stable (possibly twisted) holomorphic
vector bundle is called *projectively hyperholomorphic* if
$\mathcal{E}nd(E)$ is $\omega$-polystable hyperholomorphic.
:::

### Markman's projectively hyperholomorphic vector bundles {#secprojholo}

The starting point of [@markman] is the construction of a remarkable
class of projectively hyperholomorphic vector bundles.

::: {#example1 .construction}
*Construction 13* ([@ogrady-moduli-sheaves-hk Section 4],
[@markmanstable Section 11], [@markman Section 7]). Let $S$ be a $K3$
surface with $\mathrm{Pic}(S)=\mathbb{Z}h$ and consider an isotropic
Mukai vector $u=(r, mh, s)$ such that the moduli space $M:=M_S(u)$ is
fine and parametrises slope-stable bundles. For instance, if we assume
$\gcd(r,m)=1=\gcd(r,s)$, then by [@HL10 Corollary 4.6.7, Remark 6.1.9],
the moduli space $M$ satisfies the above-mentioned properties. By
[@Mukai2], the moduli space $M$ is a $K3$ surface and we have a
universal vector bundle $\mathcal{U}$ on $M\times S$. By conjugating
Bridgeland--King--Reid equivalence [@bridgeland-king-reid-mckay], we get
the existence of a vector bundle $\mathcal{U}^{[n]}$ on the product of
the Hilbert schemes $M^{[n]}\times S^{[n]}$. More precisely, the vector
bundle $\mathcal{U}^{[n]}$ is the Fourier--Mukai kernel of the derived
equivalence
$$\Phi_{\mathcal{U}^{[n]}}:=BKR\circ\Phi_{\mathcal{U}^{\boxtimes n}}\circ BKR^{-1}\colon \mathrm{D}^b(M^{[n]})\to \mathrm{D}^b(S^{[n]}).$$
Given $[Z]\in M^{[n]}$, corresponding to a reduced subscheme, the fiber
${\mathcal{U}^{[n]}}|_{\{[Z]\}\times S^{[n]}}$ is well understood (see
[@ogrady-moduli-sheaves-hk Section 4.3]). Recall the construction of the
isospectral Hilbert scheme, which is defined as the reduced fiber
product associated to the diagram

$$\begin{tikzcd}
    {X_n(S)} & {S^n} \\
    {S^{[n]}} & {S^{(n)}}
    \arrow["\tau"', from=1-1, to=1-2]
    \arrow["\rho", from=1-1, to=2-1]
    \arrow["\pi"', from=1-2, to=2-2]
    \arrow["\gamma", from=2-1, to=2-2]
\end{tikzcd}$$ where $\gamma$ is the Hilbert-Chow morphism and $\pi$ is
the quotient map under the action of the $n-$th symmetric group
$\Sigma_n$. Then, if $Z=\{p_1,\dots,p_n\}$ is a reduced $0$-dimensional
subscheme of $M$, we have
$${\mathcal{U}^{[n]}}|_{\{[Z]\}\times S^{[n]}}\simeq \left(\rho_*\tau^*\bigoplus_{\sigma\in\Sigma_n}E_{p_{\sigma(1)}}\boxtimes\cdots\boxtimes E_{p_{\sigma(n)}}\right)^{\Sigma_n},$$
where $E_{p_i}$ denotes the stable vector bundle corresponding to
$p_i\in M$ and the exponent $\Sigma_n$ means that we are taking the
$\Sigma_n$ invariant subsheaf with respect to the natural $\Sigma_n$
action (see [@ogrady-moduli-sheaves-hk Example 3.2.10]). In addition,
for all $[Z]\in M^{[n]}$, we have the following identities
$$\begin{align}
\mathrm{rk}\!\left({\mathcal{U}^{[n]}}|_{\{[Z]\}\times S^{[n]}}\right)
    &= r^n n!, \label{rank1}\\
c_1\!\left({\mathcal{U}^{[n]}}|_{\{[Z]\}\times S^{[n]}}\right)
    &= r^{n-1}n! \, m h
       - r^n n! \, \frac{\delta_{S^{[n]}}}{2}, \label{c11}\\
\Delta\!\left({\mathcal{U}^{[n]}}|_{\{[Z]\}\times S^{[n]}}\right)
    &= \frac{(r^n n!)^2}{12}c_2(S^{[n]}), \label{eq_modularity1}
\end{align}$$ under the decomposition
$H^2(S^{[n]},\mathbb{Z})=H^2(S,\mathbb{Z})\oplus \mathbb{Z}\delta_{S^{[n]}}$
(see [@markmanstable Lemma 11.1], [@ogrady-moduli-sheaves-hk Example
3.2.10], [@OGrady2026 Remark 2.10]). In particular, the vector bundles
${\mathcal{U}^{[n]}}|_{\{[Z]\}\times S^{[n]}}$ are modular.
:::

Next, we briefly describe the argument used by Markman in [@markman
Theorem 8.4] to construct (possibly twisted) vector bundles over any IHS
manifold of $K3^{[n]}$-type. The key will be Verbitsky's deformation of
hyperholomorphic bundles on twistor lines given in
Theorem [2](#verb){reference-type="ref" reference="verb"}, but in the
revisited form of Theorem [5](#deformingazumaya){reference-type="ref"
reference="deformingazumaya"} (see also [@markman Proposition 5.22] and
[@markman Proposition 5.15]).

We start by considering the following moduli spaces (see
[@buskin-hodge-isometry-k3] and [@markman]). Let
$\mathfrak{M}_{\Lambda}$ be the coarse moduli space parametrising marked
IHS manifolds $(X,\eta_X)$, where
$\eta_X\colon H^2(X,\mathbb{Z})\to {\Lambda}$ is an isometry. Moreover,
for any fixed rational isometry
$\phi:{\Lambda}\otimes \mathbb{Q}\to {\Lambda}\otimes \mathbb{Q}$, one
can define the moduli space $\mathfrak{M}_\phi$ of *rational Hodge
isometries*, parametrising quadruples $(X,\eta_X,Y,\eta_Y)$ such that
$(X,\eta_X),(Y,\eta_Y)\in \mathfrak{M}_{\Lambda}$ and the composition
Hodge isometry
$\psi: =\eta_Y^{-1}\circ \phi\circ \eta_X \colon H^2(X,\mathbb{Q})\to H^2(Y,\mathbb{Q})$
is a Hodge isometry sending some open subcone of the Kähler cone of $X$
into the Kähler cone of $Y$. This last condition allows us to consider
*diagonal twistor lines*. Pick
$(X,\eta_X,Y,\eta_Y)\in \mathfrak{M}_\phi$, a class
$\omega\in \mathcal{K}_X$ such that $\psi(\omega)\in \mathcal{K}_Y$ and
call $\mathcal{X} \rightarrow \mathbb{P}^1_\omega$ and
$\mathcal{Y} \rightarrow \mathbb{P}^1_{\psi(\omega)}$ the associated
twistor families. As explained in [@markman §5.3], we get an
identification of $\mathbb{P}^1_{\omega}$ with
$\mathbb{P}^1_{\psi(\omega)}$ so that
$\mathcal{X}\times_{\mathbb{P}^1}\mathcal{Y}$ is the twistor family
associated to $X\times Y$ with Kähler class
$\pi_X^*\omega+\pi_Y^*\psi(\omega)$. This definition is fundamental in
order to apply Verbitsky's result to families of sheaves. A crucial
property is:

::: {#lem_pisurj .lem}
**Lemma 14** ([@markman Lemma 5.14]). *Fix a connected component
$\mathfrak{M}_{\phi}^{\circ}$ of $\mathfrak{M}_{\phi}$. For $i=1,2$ the
natural projection morphism
$\pi_i\colon \mathfrak{M}_{\phi}^{\circ}\to \mathfrak{M}_{{\Lambda}}^{\circ}$,
defined by $\pi_i(X_1,\eta_1,X_2,\eta_2)= (X_i,\eta_i)$, is surjective
onto a connected component $\mathfrak{M}_{{\Lambda}}^{\circ}$ of
$\mathfrak{M}_{{\Lambda}}$.*
:::

By [@markman Lemma 5.8], we can connect any two points in a fixed
connected component of $\mathfrak{M}_\phi$ by a diagonal twistor path,
i.e. a connected chain of diagonal twistor lines (see [@markman
Definition 5.6]). Moreover, we can assume this path to be *generic*,
that is, we suppose the join of any two twistor lines to be points
parametrising manifolds with trivial Picard group. Choosing the
appropriate $\phi={\psi^{[n]}}$ (see Section
[1.5](#sec_vanishing_twist){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec_vanishing_twist"} for further details) and the markings,
we can consider the connected component
$\mathfrak{M}_{\psi^{[n]}}^\circ$ of $\mathfrak{M}_{\psi^{[n]}}$ that
contains $P:=(M^{[n]},\eta_{M^{[n]}},S^{[n]},\eta_{S^{[n]}})$. Now,
given any $Q:=(X,\eta_X,Y,\eta_Y)\in\mathfrak{M}^\circ_{\psi^{[n]}}$, we
can find a generic diagonal twistor path connecting $P$ to $Q$. Then,
the vector bundles $\mathcal{E}nd(\mathcal{U}^{[n]})$ flatly deform as
Azumaya algebras on those twistor paths and from them we can construct
(possibly twisted) vector bundles on $X\times Y$, unique up to twisting
by a line bundle.

More precisely, Markman considers a diagonal twistor line connecting $P$
to a point $P':=(M'^{[n]},\eta_{M'^{[n]}},S'^{[n]},\eta_{S'^{[n]}})$
consisting of a pair of marked Douady spaces with
$\mathrm{Pic}(M')=0=\mathrm{Pic}(S')$, along which $\mathcal{U}^{[n]}$
deforms as an $\overline{\omega}$-slope stable bundle, for some Kähler
class $\overline{\omega}$, then followed by a generic diagonal twistor
path from $P'$ to $Q$. Call $\mathcal{U}'^{[n]}$ the deformation of
$\mathcal{U}^{[n]}$ on $P'$, which is $\omega$-projectively
hyperholomorphic for any Kähler class $\omega$ (see [@markman Lemma 8.3]
and Definition [51](#def_proj_hyperhol){reference-type="ref"
reference="def_proj_hyperhol"}). Therefore, the vector bundle
$\mathcal{U}'^{[n]}$ can be deformed as an hyperholomorphic bundle along
any twistor line starting from $P'$. We apply this to the first twistor
line appearing in the path connecting $P'$ to $Q$. Crucially, being this
path generic, on each join of two twistor lines we obtain a (possibly
twisted) vector bundle, which is slope-stable for some Kähler class, on
a variety with trivial Picard group. It follows that such a bundle has
only trivial sub-objects; hence, it is slope-stable for all Kähler
classes. Therefore, the above argument can be iterated until we reach
$Q$. In conclusion, we get the following.

::: {#thm_compatiblevectorbundle .thm}
**Theorem 15** ([@markman],[@dequivconj Theorem 2.3]). *Given
$(X,\eta_X,Y,\eta_Y)\in\mathfrak{M}^\circ_{{\psi^{[n]}}}$ as above,
there exists a split Kähler class
$\omega_{X\times Y}:=\pi_X^*\omega_X+\pi_Y^*\omega_Y$ and a projectively
$\omega_{X\times Y}$-stable hyperholomorphic vector bundle
$(\mathcal{E},\alpha_\mathcal{E})$ such that*

1.  *$\alpha_\mathcal{E}=\left[-\frac{c_1(\mathcal{U}^{[n]})}{\mathrm{rk}(\mathcal{U}^{[n]})}\right]$,
    where we view $H^2(X\times Y,\mathbb{Z})$ as a trivial local system
    over the moduli of marked pairs;*

2.  *The twisted Fourier-Mukai transform
    $$\Phi_{\mathcal{E}}\colon \mathrm{D}^b(X,\alpha_X^{-1})\rightarrow \mathrm{D}^b(Y,\alpha_Y),$$
    with kernel $\mathcal{E}$ is an equivalence, where
    $\alpha_\mathcal{E}=\alpha_X+\alpha_Y\in \mathrm{Br}(X\times Y)=\mathrm{Br}(X)\oplus\mathrm{Br}(Y)$;*

3.  *For all $x\in X$, the Stiefel-Whitney class of the bundle on $Y$
    corresponding to $x$ is
    $$w(\mathcal{E}|_{\{x\}\times Y})=\left[\eta_Y^{-1}\left(r^{n-1}n!m\eta_S(h)-r^nn!\frac{\delta}{2}\right)\right]\in H^2(Y,\mathbb{Z}/r^nn!\mathbb{Z}).$$*
:::

The third statement follows easily from the properties in
Remark [10](#stiefel-whitney){reference-type="ref"
reference="stiefel-whitney"}. Indeed, the vector bundle $\mathcal{E}$ is
constructed deforming the Azumaya algebra
$\mathcal{E}nd(\mathcal{U}^{[n]})$, for which the Stiefel-Whitney class
is easily computed using [\[c11\]](#c11){reference-type="eqref"
reference="c11"}.

### Components of the moduli space from derived equivalences

The next standard Lemma gives a criterion for identifying the base of a
family of sheaves with a connected component of a moduli space.

::: {#lem_Ymodulisp .lem}
**Lemma 16**. *Let $X$ be a smooth projective variety and let $(Y,H)$ be
a smooth polarised variety. Let
$\Phi_{\mathcal{E}}\colon \mathrm{D}^b(X,\alpha_{X}^{-1})\to \mathrm{D}^b(Y)$
be an equivalence, where $\mathcal{E}$ is a
$\mathrm{pr}_X^*\alpha_{X}$-twisted vector bundle on $X\times Y$ such
that for every $x\in X$, the restriction $\mathcal{E}_{x}$ is Gieseker
stable with respect to $H$. Then $X$ is isomorphic to a connected
component $M_{Y,H}(\mathrm{ch}(\mathcal{E}_{x}))^{\circ}$ of the moduli
space of Gieseker $H$-semistable sheaves on $Y$ with Chern character
$\mathrm{ch}(\mathcal{E}_{x})$, for any $x\in X$.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* We show that $X$ is isomorphic to a connected component of the
moduli space $M:=M_{Y,H}\!\bigl(\mathrm{ch}(\mathcal{E}_{x})\bigr)$ of
Gieseker $H$-semistable sheaves on $Y$ with Chern character
$\mathrm{ch}(\mathcal{E}_{x})$, and that this component consists
entirely of stable vector bundles. By étale descent, the twisted family
$\mathcal{E}$ induces a morphism $f\colon X\to M$. More precisely, let
$\{U_i\}_{i\in I}$ be an étale cover of $X$ trivialising the twist
$\alpha_{X}$. Then $\mathcal{E}$ is given by data
$(\{\mathcal{E}_i\}_{i\in I},\{\varphi_{ij}\}_{i,j\in I})$, where each
$\mathcal{E}_i$ is a locally free sheaf on $U_i\times Y$ and
$\varphi_{ij}\colon\mathcal{E}_j|_{U_i\times_X U_j\times Y}\rightarrow\mathcal{E}_i|_{U_i\times_X U_j\times Y}$
are isomorphisms compatible with $\alpha_{X}$. Each $\mathcal{E}_i$
induces a classifying morphism $U_i\rightarrow M$, and hence a morphism
$g\colon U':=\coprod_i U_i\rightarrow M$. By [@Alper-StacksModuli
Proposition 3.1.7], this map descends uniquely to a morphism
$f\colon X\rightarrow M$ provided the diagram

$$\begin{tikzcd}
    {U'\times_XU'} & {U'} \\
    {U'} & M
    \arrow["{\pi_1}", from=1-1, to=1-2]
    \arrow["{\pi_2}"', from=1-1, to=2-1]
    \arrow["g", from=1-2, to=2-2]
    \arrow["g"', from=2-1, to=2-2]
\end{tikzcd}$$ commutes. This is easily verified: cover $U'\times_XU'$
by open subsets of the form $U_i\times_X U_j$, and notice that the
restriction $\mathcal{E}_i|_{U_i\times_X U_j\times Y}$ induces
$g\circ\pi_1|_{U_i\times_X U_j}$, while
$\mathcal{E}_j|_{U_i\times_X U_j\times Y}$ induces
$g\circ\pi_2|_{U_i\times_X U_j}$. Since
$\varphi_{ij}\colon\mathcal{E}_j|_{U_i\times_X U_j\times X}\rightarrow\mathcal{E}_i|_{U_i\times_X U_j\times Y}$
are isomorphisms, then
$g\circ\pi_1|_{U_i\times_X U_j}=g\circ\pi_2|_{U_i\times_X U_j}$ and the
diagram is commutative.

By [@caldararu-thesis Theorem 3.2.1], we have
$0=\mathrm{Hom}\bigl(\Phi_{\mathcal{E}}(\mathbb{C}(x)),\Phi_{\mathcal{E}}(\mathbb{C}(x'))\bigr)=\mathrm{Hom}(\mathcal{E}_x,\mathcal{E}_{x'})$
for $x\neq x'$, which implies that $f$ is injective. Since
$\mathcal{E}_x$ is $H$-stable, [@HL10 Proposition 4.5.2] yields
$$\dim T_{M,[\mathcal{E}_x]}
  = \mathrm{ext}^1(\mathcal{E}_x,\mathcal{E}_x)
  = \mathrm{ext}^1\bigl(\Phi_{\mathcal{E}}(\mathbb{C}(x)),\Phi_{\mathcal{E}}(\mathbb{C}(x))\bigr)
  = \mathrm{ext}^1\bigl(\mathbb{C}(x),\mathbb{C}(x)\bigr)
  = \dim T_{X,x},$$ where the penultimate equality follows from fully
faithfulness, and the last equality from [@Huy03 Ex. 11.9 ii)]. Thus $f$
is injective and the Zariski tangent space to $M$ has dimension
$\dim(X)$ at all points of $f(X)$. The conclusion follows by a standard
argument (see [@reede-zhang-smooth-components Lemma 1.6]). ◻
:::

### Vanishing of the Brauer classes {#sec_vanishing_twist}

In this Section we provide further details on
Construction [13](#example1){reference-type="ref" reference="example1"}
and Theorem [15](#thm_compatiblevectorbundle){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm_compatiblevectorbundle"}. In particular, in the notation
of Theorem [15](#thm_compatiblevectorbundle){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm_compatiblevectorbundle"}, we give sufficient conditions
ensuring that both $\alpha_X=0$ and $\alpha_Y=0$ (see
Lemma [18](#lem_sufficientcondition){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem_sufficientcondition"}).

As in Construction [13](#example1){reference-type="ref"
reference="example1"}, let $S$ be a $K3$ surface of Picard rank $1$ and
choose a Mukai vector $$\begin{equation}
    u=(r,mh,s)
\end{equation}$$ such that $r\geq 2$, $\gcd(r,s)=1$, $u^2=0$ and every
stable sheaf with Mukai vector $u$ is a stable vector bundle (for this
last condition, it is enough to assume $\gcd(r,m)=1$). We recall some
well-known facts (see [@Mukai2; @Yoshioka]).

The moduli space of stable vector bundles with Mukai vector $u$ is a
$K3$ surface $M$ of Picard rank $1$. We denote by $\hat{h}$ the ample
generator of $\mathrm{Pic}(M)$. There exists a universal vector bundle
$\mathcal{U}$ on $M\times S$, uniquely determined up to tensoring with
the pull-back of a line bundle $L\in \mathrm{Pic}(M)$, such that
$$\begin{equation}
\label{id_c1U}
    c_1(\mathcal{U})=k\hat{h}+mh \in H^2(M,\mathbb{Q})\oplus H^2(S,\mathbb{Q}),
\end{equation}$$ for some $k\in \mathbb{Z}$. There is a rational Hodge
isometry
$$\psi_{\mathcal{U}}\colon H^2(M,\mathbb{Q})\rightarrow H^2(S,\mathbb{Q}),$$
defined by the correspondence defined by the class
$\kappa(\mathcal{U})\sqrt{\operatorname{td}_{M\times S}}$.

Since $\gcd(r,s)=1$, we have $\psi_{\mathcal{U}^{-1}}(h)=\widehat{h}$ by
[@Yoshioka Appendix, Example 1]. Moreover, by [@Yoshioka Theorem 2.2],
the surface $S$ is also a moduli space of vector bundles on $M$ for some
Mukai vector $\widehat{u}=(r,k\widehat{h},\widehat{s})$. In particular,
the vector $\widehat{u}$ is primitive and isotropic.

::: {#lem_choosek .lem}
**Lemma 17**. *In the above setup, we can choose a universal family
$\mathcal{U}$ such that $k=(2\nu-1) m$ for some $\nu\in\mathbb{Z}$.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Since the universal family is determined up to tensoring with
the pull-back of a line bundle $L\in \mathrm{Pic}(M)$, it is enough to
show that $k\equiv(2\nu-1)m\pmod{r}$ for some $\nu\in\mathbb{Z}$.

Since $\gcd(r,m)=1$, the condition $rs=m^2(h^2/2)$ implies that $r$
divides $h^2/2$. We also have
$r\widehat{s}=k^2(\widehat{h}^2/2)=k^2(h^2/2)$ and therefore $\gcd(r,k)$
divides $\widehat{s}=\dfrac{k^2(h^2/2)}{r}=k^2\dfrac{(h^2/2)}{r}$. Thus
$\gcd(r,k)$ divides $\gcd(r,k,\widehat{s})=1$, since
$\widehat{u}=(r,k\widehat{h},\widehat{s})$ is primitive. It follows that
$\gcd(r,k)=1$.

Since $\gcd(r,m)=1$ we can find $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$ such that
$$mx+ry=k.$$ We claim that $x$ can be chosen odd. If $r$ is even, then
$\gcd(r,k)=1$ implies that $k$ is odd; hence $x$ is odd. If $r$ is odd
and $x$ is already odd, there is nothing to prove. Finally, if $r$ is
odd and $x$ is even, then $$m(x+r)+r(y-m)=k,$$ and we can replace $x$
with $x+r$, which is odd. This proves the claim. ◻
:::

As explained above, one constructs a vector bundle
$\mathcal{U}^{[n]}\in\mathrm{Coh}(M^{[n]}\times S^{[n]})$. There is
rational Hodge isometry
$\psi_{\mathcal{U}^{[n]}}:H^2(M^{[n]},\mathbb{Q})\rightarrow H^2(S^{[n]},\mathbb{Q})$:
through an important result by Taelman (see [@tae23]), it is induced by
the correspondence associated with
$\kappa(\mathcal{U}^{[n]})\sqrt{\operatorname{td}_{M^{[n]}\times S^{[n]}}}$;
we refer to [@markman Section 3.2] for further details. By [@markman
Section 7], we can decompose it as
$\psi_{\mathcal{U}^{[n]}}=(\psi_{\mathcal{U}},\mathrm{id}):H^2(M,\mathbb{Q})\oplus\mathbb{Q}\delta_{M^{[n]}}\rightarrow H^2(S,\mathbb{Q})\oplus\mathbb{Q}\delta_{S^{[n]}}$.
By Equations (7.9) and (7.10) of [@markman], we have $$\begin{equation}
    c_1(\mathcal{U}^{[n]})=a_{S^{[n]}}+a_{M^{[n]}}\in H^2(M^{[n]},\mathbb{Q})\oplus H^2(S^{[n]},\mathbb{Q}),
\end{equation}$$ where $$\begin{align}
    a_{S^{[n]}}&=r^{n-1}n!mh
       - r^n n!\frac{\delta_{S^{[n]}}}{2},\\
    a_{M^{[n]}}&=r^{n-1}n!k\widehat{h}+r^n n!\frac{\delta_{M^{[n]}}}{2}.
\end{align}$$ It is straightforward to get the following relation:
$$\begin{equation}
\label{eq_identifyingcomponents}
    a_{M^{[n]}}=\frac{k}{m}\psi_{\mathcal{U}^{[n]}}^{-1}\left(a_{S^{[n]}}\right)+\frac{r^nn!(k+m)}{2m}\delta_{M^{[n]}}
\end{equation}$$

Moreover, in the setup of Theorem
[15](#thm_compatiblevectorbundle){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm_compatiblevectorbundle"}, we have the Brauer classes
$$\begin{align}
    \alpha_X&=\left[-\dfrac{1}{r^nn!}\eta_X^{-1}\circ\eta_{M^{[n]}}(a_{M^{[n]}})\right]\in\mathrm{Br}(X)=H^2(X,\mathbb{Z})/\mathrm{Pic}(X)\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}\label{eq_twistonX}\\
    \alpha_Y&=\left[-\dfrac{1}{r^nn!}\eta_Y^{-1}\circ\eta_{S^{[n]}}(a_{S^{[n]}})\right]\in\mathrm{Br}(Y)=H^2(Y,\mathbb{Z})/\mathrm{Pic}(Y)\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}\label{eq_twistonY}
\end{align}$$ By construction, following the notation of
Theorem [15](#thm_compatiblevectorbundle){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm_compatiblevectorbundle"}, following diagram commutes:

$$\begin{equation}
\label{commutation_markings}
    \begin{tikzcd}
    {H^2(X,\mathbb{Q})} & {H^2(Y,\mathbb{Q})} \\
    {\Lambda_{K3^{[n]},\mathbb{Q}}} & {\Lambda_{K3^{[n]},\mathbb{Q}}} \\
    {H^2(M^{[n]},\mathbb{Q})} & {H^2(S^{[n]},\mathbb{Q})}
    \arrow["{\psi_{\mathcal{E}}}", from=1-1, to=1-2]
    \arrow["{\eta_X}"', from=1-1, to=2-1]
    \arrow["{\eta_Y}", from=1-2, to=2-2]
    \arrow["{\psi^{[n]}}", from=2-1, to=2-2]
    \arrow["{\eta_{M^{[n]}}}", from=3-1, to=2-1]
    \arrow["{\psi_{\mathcal{U}^{[n]}}}"', from=3-1, to=3-2]
    \arrow["{\eta_{S^{[n]}}}"', from=3-2, to=2-2]
\end{tikzcd}
\end{equation}$$

Combining [\[eq_twistonX\]](#eq_twistonX){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq_twistonX"} with
[\[eq_identifyingcomponents\]](#eq_identifyingcomponents){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq_identifyingcomponents"}, and using the commutativity of
diagram [\[commutation_markings\]](#commutation_markings){reference-type="eqref"
reference="commutation_markings"}, we obtain $$\begin{align}
    \alpha_X&=\left[-\frac{k}{m r^nn!}\psi_{\mathcal{E}}^{-1}\circ\eta_{Y}^{-1}\circ \eta_{S^{[n]}}(a_{S^{[n]}})-\frac{(k+m)}{2m}\eta_X^{-1}\circ\eta_{M^{[n]}}(\delta_{M^{[n]}})\right]\label{eq_twistX}
\end{align}$$

A crucial step in the proof of Theorem
[37](#thm_main){reference-type="ref" reference="thm_main"} will be to
choose the markings in such a way that the Brauer class $\alpha_Y$
vanishes, so that the kernel $\mathcal{E}$ parametrises untwisted vector
bundles. For this purpose, we prove the following

::: {#lem_sufficientcondition .lem}
**Lemma 18**. *Assume that $\frac{k+m}{2m}\in\mathbb{Z}$ and
$\eta_{Y}^{-1}\circ \eta_{S^{[n]}}(a_{S^{[n]}})\in\mathrm{Pic}(Y)_{\mathbb{Q}}$.
Then $\alpha_Y=0$ and $\alpha_X=0$.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The vanishing of $\alpha_Y$ follows immediately from
[\[eq_twistonY\]](#eq_twistonY){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq_twistonY"}. On the other hand, by
[\[eq_twistX\]](#eq_twistX){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq_twistX"}, the class $\alpha_X$ is represented by
$-\frac{k}{mr^nn!}\psi_{\mathcal{E}}^{-1}\circ\eta_{Y}^{-1}\circ \eta_{S^{[n]}}(a_{S^{[n]}})-\frac{(k+m)}{2m}\eta_X^{-1}\circ\eta_{M^{[n]}}(\delta_{M^{[n]}})$.
Since
$-\frac{(k+m)}{2m}\eta_X^{-1}\circ\eta_{M^{[n]}}(\delta_{M^{[n]}})\in H^2(X,\mathbb{Z})$,
this has the same Brauer class as
$-\frac{k}{m r^nn!}\psi_{\mathcal{E}}^{-1}\circ\eta_{Y}^{-1}\circ \eta_{S^{[n]}}(a_{S^{[n]}})$.
This class is zero because $\psi_{\mathcal{E}}^{-1}$ is Hodge and
$\eta_Y^{-1}\circ \eta_{S^{[n]}}(a_{S^{[n]}})\in \mathrm{Pic}(Y)_\mathbb{Q}$. ◻
:::

::: {#rmk_nicotranquillo .rmk}
*Remark 19*. By Lemma [17](#lem_choosek){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem_choosek"}, we can always assume that
$\frac{k+m}{2m}\in\mathbb{Z}$.
:::

The Example below shows that the vanishing of $\alpha_Y$ is not enough
to conclude automatically that $\alpha_X=0$.

::: {#ex_nonfinemoduli .example}
*Example 20*. Let $S$ be a very general polarised $K3$ surface of degree
$4$, i.e. $\mathrm{Pic}(S)=\mathbb{Z}h$ and $h^2=4$. Let $M=M_S(u)$ be
the moduli $K3$ surface parametrising stable vector bundles with Mukai
vector $u=(2,h,1)$. By Lemma [17](#lem_choosek){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem_choosek"} and identity
([\[id_c1U\]](#id_c1U){reference-type="ref" reference="id_c1U"}), we can
choose a universal family $\mathcal{U}\in\mathrm{Coh}(M\times S)$, so
that $c_1(\mathcal{U})=\widehat{h}+h$.

Choose a class $\gamma\in H^2(S,\mathbb{Z})$ such that $\gamma^2=0$ and
$\gamma\cdot h=1$; this can always be done, as $H^2(S,\mathbb{Z})$
contains at least a copy of the hyperbolic plane (see Section
[2.1.2](#sec_k3nlattice){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec_k3nlattice"}). Set
$w:=h-\delta_{S^{[2]}}+2\gamma\in H^2(S^{[2]},\mathbb{Z})$. Then $w$ is
primitive and $w^2>0$. Fix a marking
$\eta_S\colon H^2(S,\mathbb{Z})\rightarrow\Lambda_{K3}$, inducing a
marking $\eta_{S^{[2]}}$ of $S^{[2]}$. By surjectivity of the period
map, there exists a projective marked IHS manifold of $K3^{[2]}$-type
$(Y,\eta_Y)$ with period $\sigma_Y\in w^\perp$ and with
$\mathrm{Pic}(Y)=\mathbb{Z}\eta_Y^{-1}\circ\eta_{S^{[2]}}(w)$, such that
$(S^{[2]},\eta_{S^{[2]}})$ and $(Y, \eta_Y)$ belong to the same
connected component of $\mathfrak{M}_{\Lambda_{K3^{[2]}}}$. Combining
the previous relations, we obtain $$\begin{align*}
    \alpha_Y=\left[-\dfrac{1}{2^22!}\eta_Y^{-1}\circ\eta_{S^{[2]}}(a_{S^{[2]}})\right]=\left[-\frac{1}{2}\eta_Y^{-1}\circ\eta_{S^{[2]}}\left(w\right)+\eta_Y^{-1}\circ\eta_{S^{[2]}}\left(\gamma\right)\right]=0,
\end{align*}$$ where the last equality follows from the observation that
$-\frac{1}{2}\eta_Y^{-1}\circ\eta_{S^{[2]}}\left(w\right)+\eta_Y^{-1}\circ\eta_{S^{[2]}}\left(\gamma\right)\in\mathrm{Pic}(Y)_{\mathbb{Q}}+H^2(Y,\mathbb{Z})$.
By Lemma [14](#lem_pisurj){reference-type="ref" reference="lem_pisurj"},
there exists a marked IHS manifold $(X,\eta_X)$ of $K3^{[n]}-$type such
that we can apply Theorem
[15](#thm_compatiblevectorbundle){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm_compatiblevectorbundle"} to the pair
$(X,\eta_X,Y,\eta_Y)$. On the other hand, we obtain $$\begin{align*}
\alpha_X
&= \left[-\frac{1}{8}\eta_X^{-1}\circ\eta_{M^{[2]}}\circ\psi_{\mathcal{U}^{[2]}}^{-1}\left(a_{S^{[2]}}\right)-\eta_X^{-1}\circ\eta_{M^{[2]}}\left(\delta_{M^{[2]}}\right)\right] 
&& \text{by Equation~\eqref{eq_twistX}} \\
&= \left[-\frac{1}{8}\eta_X^{-1}\circ\eta_{M^{[2]}}\circ\psi_{\mathcal{U}^{[2]}}^{-1}\left(a_{S^{[2]}}\right)\right]
&& \text{since } \eta_X^{-1}\circ\eta_{M^{[2]}}\left(\delta_{M^{[n]}}\right)\in H^2(X,\mathbb{Z}) \\
&= \left[-\frac{1}{2}\psi_{\mathcal{E}}^{-1}\circ\eta_Y^{-1}\circ\eta_{S^{[2]}}\left(w\right)+\eta_X^{-1}\circ\eta_{M^{[2]}}\circ\psi_{\mathcal{U}^{[2]}}^{-1}(\gamma)\right]
&& \text{by the definitions of $\gamma$ and $w$} \\
&= \left[\eta_X^{-1}\circ\eta_{M^{[2]}}\circ\psi_{\mathcal{U}^{[2]}}^{-1}(\gamma)\right]
&& \text{since }\frac{1}{2}\psi_{\mathcal{E}}^{-1}\circ\eta_Y^{-1}\circ\eta_{S^{[2]}}\left(w\right)\in\mathrm{Pic}(X).
\end{align*}$$

We now show that this class is non-zero in $\mathrm{Br}(X)$. Suppose,
for contradiction, that $\alpha_X=0$. Then $$\begin{equation*}
    \eta_X^{-1}\circ\eta_{M^{[2]}}\circ\psi_{\mathcal{U}^{[2]}}^{-1}(\gamma)\in\mathrm{Pic}(X)_\mathbb{Q}+H^2(X,\mathbb{Z}).
\end{equation*}$$ Applying
$\psi_{\mathcal{U}^{[2]}}\circ\eta_{M^{[2]}}^{-1}\circ\eta_X$, and using
the description of $\mathrm{Pic}(X)$, we obtain
$$\gamma\in \psi_{\mathcal{U}^{[2]}}\bigl(H^2(M^{[2]},\mathbb{Z})\bigr)+\mathbb{Q}w.$$
Hence there exists $\lambda\in\mathbb{Q}$ such that $$\begin{equation*}
   \gamma-\lambda w=(1-2\lambda)\gamma-\lambda h+\lambda\delta_{S^{[n]}}\in \psi_{\mathcal{U}^{[2]}}\bigl(H^2(M^{[2]},\mathbb{Z})\bigr).
\end{equation*}$$ Since
$\psi_{\mathcal{U}^{[2]}}=(\psi_{\mathcal{U}},\mathrm{id})$, it follows
that $\lambda\in\mathbb{Z}$. We get $$\begin{equation}
\label{eq:odd}
   h\cdot\bigl((1-2\lambda)\gamma-\lambda h+\lambda\delta_{S^{[n]}}\bigr)
   =(1-2\lambda)h\cdot\gamma-\lambda h^2
   =1-2\lambda-4\lambda
   =1-6\lambda.
\end{equation}$$ This is odd for every $\lambda\in\mathbb{Z}$. On the
other hand, by the definition of $\psi_{\mathcal{U}}$, for every
$\beta\in H^2(S,\mathbb{Z})$ one has $$\begin{equation*}
    \beta\in \psi_{\mathcal{U}}(H^2(M,\mathbb{Z}))\iff h\cdot\beta\in 2\mathbb{Z},
\end{equation*}$$ contradicting
[\[eq:odd\]](#eq:odd){reference-type="eqref" reference="eq:odd"}. This
proves $\alpha_X\neq 0$.
:::
